pr_title: Add a "debug tap" that lets you see the VT behind a connection
pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

This pull request adds a debugging feature that can be activated by holding down <kbd>Left Alt</kbd> _and_ <kbd>Right Alt</kbd> when a new tab is being created.

That debugging feature takes the form of a split pane that shows the raw VT sequences being written to and received from the connection.

It looks like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14316954/77599489-1009a600-6ec2-11ea-995a-8e5531df2dcb.png)

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #3206

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

When those buttons are held down, every connection that's created as part of a new tab is wrapped and split into _two_ connections: one to capture input (and stand in for the main connection) and one to capture output (and be displayed off to the side)

## Validation

This has been baking in various forms of validation since September.
pr_comments:
Closing the debug tap side doesn't cause any issues (input and output still work). Closing the "main" side terminates both.

If you hold down alt-alt while launching terminal, you can even trigger a tap on the initial connection.

I like it but two thoughts:

1. Isn't Alt Gr (mapped on right alt on some keyboards) simulated with left alt and right ctrl? Does the keyboard check for right alt only detect a true right alt key or will it also detect the simulation? Not sure if this is important... 

2. Can it be completely deactivated by default and require a global setting in your settings file of like debugTools: true before it has the chance of turning on? I imagine someone out there is going to press both alts for giggles and not expect this to happen. I'd also name the setting in a generic way so we can just make all debug tools available with one setting.
_Personally_, I'd prefer a keybinding that isn't set by default. Then my wonky keyboard can do it. But that sounds like pointer bindings to me :(
I disagree that this should be a key binding. It’s not an action, it’s a modifier to _a whole bunch of actions_ (making a new tab, launching the terminal, opening a specific profile).

> 1. Isn't Alt Gr (mapped on right alt on some keyboards) simulated with left alt and right ctrl? Does the keyboard check for right alt only detect a true right alt key or will it also detect the simulation? Not sure if this is important...

I imagine someone out there is going to press both alts for giggles and not expect this to happen. Yeah, definitely.
@miniksa alright, `debugFeatures` it is, and it defaults to `true` if `_DEBUG` and `false` if release

review_comments: This won't work during startup with a bunch of commands (I think we'll just evaluate the `Automatic` as `Vertical`), but considering this is a debug tool I'm okay with that
I hate to be _that_ guy. But could we add this to the docs?

I'm more thinking _this is a feature we tell people to enable, then they turn it off_. I don't want to put it in the docs because adding the _key_ versus adding _features that depend_ on the key are two separate operations. We're practically guaranteed to only update the docs once.

I'm (almost?) to the point where I'd rather not have a debugging feature that'll help us if it means writing up a bunch of user-facing documentation, fwiw. The docs can come after, if we deem them necessary and if we do start using this in field diagnostics.
